findings.location: Line 44-46, custom button control with id "s3-customcontrol"
findings.violation: This div has role="button" and tabindex="0" to make it focusable and announce as a button, but there is no onclick event handler or keyboard event listener. Users who navigate with keyboard and press Enter or Space will not activate the button's function.
findings.fix: Add an onclick event handler and a keyboard event listener (or use a native <button> element instead of a div).

findings.violation: The input has aria-invalid="true" indicating an error state, but there is no aria-errormessage or aria-describedby attribute connecting it to the error message on line 68. Screen readers will announce the invalid state but not the explanation of what is wrong.
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" to the input element to link it to the error message.

findings.location: Line 64-65, phone number field label and input
findings.violation: The label text includes "(required)" indicating this is a required field, but the input element itself lacks the required attribute. This creates an inconsistency where the visual label and the HTML semantics do not match.
findings.fix: Add the required attribute to the <input> element, or remove "(required)" from the label text and rely on the required attribute alone.

Choose a plan
Enter payment details

findings.violation: The wizard-steps container and individual step divs lack semantic structure or ARIA attributes to convey that this is a step indicator. Screen reader users cannot understand the purpose of this component or which step is currently active.
findings.fix: Add role="list" to the wizard-steps div and role="listitem" to each step div, or use <ol> and <li>. Add aria-current="step" to the active step and use aria-label to indicate the step number and total (e.g., "Step 1 of 3").

findings.violation: The alt text mentions "parking spaces" but the image filename is "platform-update.jpg", suggesting the image shows a platform, not parking spaces. The mismatch between filename and alt text content indicates the alt text may not accurately describe the image.
findings.fix: Verify what the image actually shows and update the alt text to accurately describe the image content.
